analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop.swift head lines 1-1220. The changes are limited to head 724-735, which add selectedModelRecovery, selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride (a test seam that is nil in production), savedEnabledModels and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch, and head 897, which seeds savedEnabledModels from config.backend.enabledModels.

These fields hold operator model-selection state for status reporting and model recovery. They do not touch keyPair/X25519 (A-003), the attestation signer, modelHashes/liveModelHashes (T-012/T-027), App Attest authorization (TB-011/T-053), the add-on hold (TB-012) or prefix-cache scoping (T-041).

DaemonState+Coding.swift (unit b07e74f6c3b43562:0) carries metadata only; its source text was not supplied. Per the patch excerpt, it adds optional encode/decode keys enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch and selectedModelRecovery. These are model IDs in the owner-local daemon state file, which already exposes advertisedModels and servingSelection, so I see no new secret exposure.

Open questions for the integration pass:
(1) SelectedModelRecovery (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift, not supplied) does a no-eviction reload of selected models. It should be checked that it respects add-on hold fences (T-059 model-load fence), drain/update admission, retiringModels and failedSelfTestHashes, so that a model that failed its self-test or is held cannot reload.
(2) Whether the CLI decoding of the state file treats these fields as advisory only. The state file is operator-writable (TB-003), so it must not drive serving decisions.

Neither question is evidenced as a regression in the supplied units.
